This is a rather hot function that is called with a potentially NULL
struct common_audit_data"" pointer argument.  And in that case it has to
provide and initialize its own dummy common_audit_data structure.
However
column2: all the _common_ cases already pass it a real audit-data

column1: structure
column2: so that uncommon NULL case not only creates a silly run-time

column1: test
column2: more importantly it causes that function to have a big stack frame

column1: for the dummy variable that isn't even used in the common case!
So get rid of that stupid run-time behavior
functions that currently call with a NULL pointer just call a new helper
function instead (naturally called inode_has_perm_noapd()
no adp argument).
This makes the run-time test be a static code generation issue instead
and allows for a much denser stack since none of the common callers need
the dummy structure.  And a denser stack not only means less stack space
usage
column2: it means better cache behavior.  So we have a win-win-win from

column1: this simplification: less code executed
better cache behavior.
